items.summary_original: PAHO secures first-ever region-wide access agreements for HPV testing across Latin America and the Caribbean, with support from Unitaid Oscar Reyes 11 Nov 2026
items.summary_ai_original: Washington, D.C./Geneva, 11 November 2026 — Millions of women across Latin America and the Caribbean will gain access to more affordable, high-quality human papillomavirus (HPV) testing under landmark regional access agreements negotiated by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) through its Regional Revolving Fun
items.article_text_original: Landmark regional agreements will lower costs of high-quality HPV testing and help more women benefit from effective cervical cancer screening. Washington, D.C./Geneva, 11 November 2026 — Millions of women across Latin America and the Caribbean will gain access to more affordable, high-quality human papillomavirus (HPV) testing under landmark regional access agreements negotiated by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) through its Regional Revolving Funds. Unitaid supported these efforts to expand access to HPV testing and will advance implementation activities in selected countries. HPV infection causes nearly all cases of cervical cancer, which kills more than 40,000 women in the region each year. Cervical cancer is highly preventable through vaccination, screening and timely treatment. Until now, countries across Latin America and the Caribbean have faced some of the highest HPV test prices in the world. Under these first-ever regional access agreements, countries will be able to access high-quality molecular HPV tests through preferential pricing and a comprehensive support package, with participating countries expected to realize cost savings ranging from 30% to 70%. These technologies are now available through PAHO's Revolving Fund under harmonized regional conditions for all countries and territories in Latin America and the Caribbean. The arrangements expand the range of WHO-recommended molecular HPV testing technologies available through PAHO's Revolving Funds. In addition to access to testing, the agreements include implementation support, equipment access, training, maintenance and technical assistance designed to facilitate country adoption and scale-up. By building these components together, the agreements help to reduce operational barriers that have often limited the introduction of new diagnostic technologies. PAHO/WHO has recommended the use of HPV testing in cervical cancer screening programs since 2013, with updated guidance issued in 2026. However, uptake in the region has been limited due to financial, technical, and programmatic barriers. Unitaid's support to PAHO translates into expanded access to HPV testing in the region. Unitaid will also support implementation activities in El Salvador, Guatemala, Grenada, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, and Saint Lucia, helping countries to introduce or expand HPV-based screening programs while strengthening follow-up care for women with positive results. "Through PAHO's Revolving Funds, countries now have access to high-quality HPV testing under more favorable conditions, helping accelerate efforts to eliminate cervical cancer in the Americas," said PAHO Director Dr. Jarbas Barbosa. "These agreements reflect PAHO's commitment to working with Member States and partners to expand equitable access to essential health technologies and strengthen cervical cancer prevention programs across the Region." “These agreements build on Unitaid’s global efforts to make cervical cancer prevention more affordable and accessible for women everywhere,” said Dr. Philippe Duneton, Executive Director of Unitaid. “By expanding access to affordable, high-quality HPV testing in Latin America and the Caribbean, and extending favorable pricing to countries that have historically been excluded from such arrangements, this initiative helps accelerate progress toward cervical cancer elimination while creating a more equitable and sustainable market for screening technologies.” Molecular tests directly detect high-risk HPV types responsible for most cervical cancer cases, allowing for early identification of women at risk. Compared to other screening methods, they perform better and can use self-collected samples, which can help expand access to testing among underserved populations. The ESTAMPA study, conducted in Latin America, found that HPV testing detected nearly all cases of precancerous cervical lesions and invasive cancer, while cytology, the conventional screening method, identified fewer than half of the cases. This highlights significant gaps between the accuracy of these two methods. Expanding the use of HPV tests is key to advancing toward the WHO’s global cervical cancer elimination targets – known as the 90-70-90 goals: 90% of girls vaccinated against HPV, 70% of women screened with a high-performance test, and 90% of women with lesions appropriately treated. Currently, 16 countries and territories in Latin America and the Caribbean have introduced HPV testing in their screening programs, although coverage has been limited by the high cost of the tests. The new access to molecular HPV tests through the Revolving Funds is part of PAHO’s Disease Elimination Initiative, which seeks to eliminate more than 30 diseases and related conditions in the Americas, including cervical cancer. It also forms part of the Better Care for NCDs initiative, designed to strengthen health systems and integrate prevention and control of these diseases into primary care. Unitaid’s cervical cancer elimination efforts in Latin America are made possible through contributions from the Government of Japan, alongside support from Unitaid’s other core donors Brazil, Chile, France, the Gates Foundation, Norway, Portugal, the Republic of Korea, Spain and the United Kingdom. About PAHO The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) works with the countries of the Americas to improve the health and quality of life of its population. Founded in 1902, it is the world’s oldest international public health agency. It serves as the Regional Office of WHO for the Americas and is the specialized health agency of the Inter-American system (OAS). For more information about PAHO and its work, please visit: www.paho.org About Unitaid Unitaid saves lives by making new health products affordable and available in low- and middle-income countries. Collaborating with partners, Unitaid identifies innovative treatments, tackles market barriers, and quickly delivers solutions to those in need. Since 2006, Unitaid has unlocked over 150 health products, addressing HIV, TB, malaria, women’s and children’s health, and pandemic preparedness. Every year, these products benefit more than 300 million people. Unitaid is a hosted partnership of the World Health Organization. www.unitaid.org Media contacts PAHO: Sebastian Oliel: +1 202 316-5679 / Ashley Baldwin: + 1 202 340-4025 - mediateam@paho.org Unitaid: Kyle Wilkinson, +41 79 445 17 45, wilkinsonk@unitaid.who.int

items.article_text_original: Washington, D.C., 6 November 2026 (PAHO) – With Pope Leo XIV due to visit Argentina, Uruguay and Peru from 6 to 17 November, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) is encouraging travelers, pilgrims and people attending large religious gatherings to take precautions against measles. The Americas are experiencing a resurgence of measles, with 57,666 confirmed cases and 81 deaths reported in 17 countries and territories between January and 31 October 2026 – 4.7 times the number recorded during the same period in 2025. PAHO has published a guide with health recommendations for travelers and pilgrims, including advice on vaccination and measures to reduce the risk of infection and transmission during travel and mass gatherings. Travelers are encouraged to read the guide and check that their measles vaccination is up to date before travelling.

items.article_text_original: Madrid, November 5, 2026 (PAHO) – The Director of the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), Dr. Jarbas Barbosa, called for health to be placed among the political and diplomatic priorities of Ibero-America during a series of high-level meetings held in Madrid on the sidelines of the XXX Ibero-American Summit of Heads of State and Government. During the High-Level Political Dialogue with Ibero-American Foreign Ministers, held on November 3, Dr. Barbosa called for stronger investment and partnerships in health, highlighting their contribution to stability, economic development, and the well-being of populations. “Health is no longer an issue exclusively for ministries of health. It is now a priority for foreign policy, security, and development,” he said. Speaking to foreign ministers and representatives of the 22 countries that make up the Ibero-American Community, the PAHO Director also stressed the need to follow through on the commitments made at the XVII Ibero-American Conference of Ministers of Health, held in May 2026. These include emergency preparedness, equitable access to health technologies, mental health, and strengthening the health workforce. He also highlighted PAHO’s cooperation with the Ibero-American General Secretariat (SEGIB) and Ibero-American health networks to advance joint initiatives on disease elimination, access to medicines, and capacity-building. New partnerships to strengthen health cooperation As part of its agenda in Madrid, PAHO and the Mundo Sano Foundation co-hosted the high-level dialogue “Global Health on the Ibero-American Agenda: Cooperation, Coordination, and Success Stories” at Casa de América. The event brought together representatives of governments, international organizations, the private sector, and civil society to explore opportunities to expand Ibero-American cooperation initiatives, including the “No Baby with Chagas” program and the Ibero-American Disability Program. The PAHO Director also signed a cooperation agreement with Grupo Social ONCE to improve access to health services and remove barriers faced by people with disabilities in Latin America and the Caribbean, in line with the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. PAHO and the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID) also signed a declaration of intent to work toward a new cooperation agreement aimed at strengthening health systems. The proposed collaboration includes initiatives in maternal and child health, the elimination of communicable diseases, immunization, epidemiological surveillance, and health emergency preparedness and response. Through these meetings and agreements, PAHO aims to strengthen cooperation with countries, SEGIB, and international partners, and help translate political commitments into tangible health improvements for people across the Americas.
